Import the shared records from `@clossys/designer/components`. Import navigation and selection from `@clossys/designer/catalog`. The components barrel remains client-only; charts render through the existing `@clossys/designer/charts` entry point. No new package subpath is introduced.

46 legacy guidance records appear once below. Navigation follows 6 authoritative IA groups and 27 families with canonical leaf IDs. Unregistered legacy guidance appears separately, outside navigation.

Stable purpose, content and anatomy are separate from medium-specific implementation. Web cites current source; email, print and video are unassessed. Import safety, server rendering and visual resemblance establish no other medium’s support.

Represented scalar options are a bounded source-checked selection, not an exhaustive inherited API or a Cartesian product. Defaults distinguish local initializers, inherited peer behavior and omitted/conditional values. Data, compound parts, callbacks, style and arbitrary children are authored inputs rather than selectable configuration axes.

`COMPONENT_COMPARISON` declares preferred finite columns and optional rows for comparison; `maxCells` equals their product at no more than 24. `ComponentComparison` describes this data-only contract. Its `constraints` references original rules; `constraintPolicy: "skip-violations"` skips only `requires`, `exclusive` and `paired` violations with complete authored inputs. Applicability (`effective-when`), ignored-option, `derived` and `data` rules never skip cells. Components without finite options have no comparison entry.

Consumer-owned demonstration coverage is unassessed here. A fixed controlled value or a single option cannot demonstrate toggling or switching. Runtime acceptance, visual effectiveness and type/runtime rejection differ. Token evidence is partial and distinguishes direct reads from transitive bindings; importing a helper does not consume all its tokens.

## Component reference

### Actions

#### Buttons

##### `act.button` — Button

- Purpose: Carry out one named action.
- Use when: The reader is ready to submit, confirm or change something.
- Avoid when: The intent is to travel to a destination rather than perform an action.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Link for navigation; IconButton for a compact, clearly named secondary control.
- Content: Write a short verb phrase that describes the resulting action.
- Anatomy: One action label, with an optional subordinate visual cue.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned form block, place a submit Button after the fields.
- Accessibility: Keep the action name understandable without relying on its fill or icon.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `act.icon-button` — IconButton

- Purpose: Carry out a compact action represented by a familiar glyph.
- Use when: Space is constrained and the action can still be named clearly.
- Avoid when: The control is the primary action of a page or the glyph needs explanation.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Button for a visible verb label; use Link for a destination.
- Content: Supply a concise action name and one glyph with the same meaning.
- Anatomy: One action glyph and its equivalent accessible name.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned carousel block, use named previous and next IconButtons.
- Accessibility: The required label names the control; its inner glyph remains decorative.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

#### Menus

##### `act.menu` — Menu

- Purpose: Offer a compact collection of actions from one trigger.
- Use when: Several related commands should be revealed on demand.
- Avoid when: The content is an input choice set or a rich explanatory panel.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Select for choosing a value; Popover for arbitrary panel content.
- Content: Name the trigger and each command. Use Menu.Section for a real section heading and separators between groups.
- Anatomy: One trigger and a repeated collection of actionable items, optionally grouped in Menu.Section with a real heading.
- Block composition example: AccountMenu composes Menu.Item commands and Menu.Section preference groups with an actor trigger.
- Accessibility: Name the trigger and each section. Section headings use the menu primitive's Header; section selection provides menuitemcheckbox preferences. Disabled items and keyboard navigation belong to the primitive.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

### Inputs

#### Form

##### `enter.field` — Field

- Purpose: Associate a label and supporting messages with a custom control.
- Use when: The control has no dedicated labelled field component in this package.
- Avoid when: A supplied TextField, Select or other labelled component already owns this wiring.
- Alternatives and boundary: Prefer the dedicated input component when available; Field supplies wiring rather than an input.
- Content: Write a control label, an optional instruction and a specific validation message.
- Anatomy: A label, one custom value control and optional helper and error messages.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned signature block, spread Field’s generated wiring onto the actual input control.
- Accessibility: The consumer must apply the generated ID and ARIA properties to the correct focusable control.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

#### Text

##### `enter.search-field` — SearchField

- Purpose: Collect a query that narrows or finds content.
- Use when: Typing a query and clearing it are part of the same search task.
- Avoid when: The value is ordinary form data with no search meaning.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use TextField for stored text; ComboBox for searching a fixed choice set.
- Content: Name what can be searched and give helpful query instructions when needed.
- Anatomy: A query entry with a clear affordance when the query is nonempty.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned results-toolbar block, connect SearchField to the results query.
- Accessibility: The clear action must remain keyboard reachable and return attention to the query.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `enter.text-field` — TextField

- Purpose: Collect one line of free-form text.
- Use when: The answer is a short textual value with optional guidance or validation.
- Avoid when: The answer needs several paragraphs, date segments or a predefined option list.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Textarea for long text, DateField for dates, or Select for fixed choices.
- Content: Supply a persistent field label; helper and error text should explain the expected value.
- Anatomy: A label, a single value entry and optional supporting messages.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned contact-form block, pair a name TextField with submit controls.
- Accessibility: A placeholder never replaces the label or its association with the input.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

#### Choice

##### `enter.checkbox` — Checkbox

- Purpose: Mark a selection that can be committed with other choices.
- Use when: One or more independent selections form part of a larger task.
- Avoid when: A setting should take effect immediately or choices are mutually exclusive.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Switch for immediate settings; RadioGroup for choosing exactly one option.
- Content: Describe the selection in a visible label rather than only marking the box.
- Anatomy: A binary selection mark and its label, optionally a mixed aggregate state.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned bulk-actions block, derive checked and mixed state from selected rows.
- Accessibility: Mixed is a separate presentational state; it does not set the underlying selection.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `enter.combo-box` — ComboBox

- Purpose: Choose one value by typing to narrow a known option set.
- Use when: The list is large enough that filtering reduces scanning effort.
- Avoid when: The task is open-ended search without a selected option identity.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Select for a short closed list; SearchField for finding external results.
- Content: Provide stable option IDs, readable labels and textValue for complex labels.
- Anatomy: A labelled editable query, suggestion trigger and filtered repeated options.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned assignment block, use ComboBox to find an assignee from known people.
- Accessibility: Keep focus in the input while navigating suggestions and name the suggestion trigger.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `enter.radio-group` — RadioGroup

- Purpose: Choose one value while keeping a small option set visible.
- Use when: Side-by-side comparison of mutually exclusive options aids the decision.
- Avoid when: The list is too large to scan or independent selections are allowed.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Select for compact choice; Checkbox for independent options.
- Content: Name the group and each choice; optional per-choice descriptions explain differences.
- Anatomy: One group label and repeated mutually exclusive labelled choices.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned preference-selection block, render at least two RadioGroup.Radio choices.
- Accessibility: Use the group’s label and roving keyboard selection; orientation aligns option layout and keyboard navigation.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `inform.banner` — Banner

- Use when: Information or a warning belongs in the normal content flow until the reader responds.

- Use when: Content needs a shared ground distinct from its surrounding section.
- Avoid when: The surface needs interaction semantics supplied automatically.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use a consumer-owned card block for named heading, body and actions; Link or Button for actual interaction.
- Content: Keep the content hierarchy meaningful within the surface rather than relying on the border.
- Anatomy: One containing content surface whose treatment follows its context.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned summary-card block, compose Card with a heading, metric and action.
- Accessibility: A Card is not inherently interactive or a landmark; add appropriate semantics through composition.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `group.separator` — Separator

- Purpose: Mark a boundary between neighboring groups of content.
- Use when: A subtle rule improves grouping without adding another content surface.
- Avoid when: Spacing alone already explains the structure or the rule is mistaken for content.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Card for a containing surface; use spacing within a consumer-owned block for weak grouping.
- Content: A separator carries no authored message; the adjacent groups provide its meaning.
- Anatomy: One horizontal or vertical boundary, optionally purely decorative.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned toolbar block, use decorative Separator between related action groups.
- Accessibility: Mark decorative boundaries hidden; a semantic separator keeps the corresponding orientation.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `reveal.disclosure` — Disclosure

- Purpose: Reveal or hide one section while retaining its place in the document.
- Use when: Supplementary content can be expanded without opening a separate overlay.
- Avoid when: The task needs mutually exclusive panels or a coordinated accordion controller.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Tabs for peer panels; a consumer-owned accordion block for coordinated disclosures.
- Content: Name the expandable section with a title that predicts its contents.
- Anatomy: One persistent section trigger and its expandable content.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned FAQ block, repeat Disclosure for independently expandable answers.
- Accessibility: Preserve the trigger-to-panel association and expanded state; hidden content remains part of the disclosure.

#### Overlays

##### `reveal.dialog` — Dialog

- Purpose: Focus attention on a modal task that temporarily suspends the page.
- Use when: The reader needs to finish or dismiss a bounded task before returning.
- Avoid when: The information can remain inline or is merely a short description.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Disclosure for inline content; Popover for an anchored task; Tooltip for a short description.
- Content: Supply a clear dialog heading and purposeful task content through the content slot.
- Anatomy: An opening trigger, a modal content surface and a dismissal path.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned confirmation block, compose Dialog.Heading, the explanation and explicit action controls.
- Accessibility: Retain focus containment, Escape dismissal and focus return; use Dialog.Heading for the content name.
- Demonstration coverage: unassessed. Consumer-owned fixtures and interaction evidence have not been assessed here. A supported package option is not proof of a working catalog demonstration.

##### `reveal.popover` — Popover

- Purpose: Reveal an anchored panel for a small contextual task.
- Use when: A rich preview or compact form should remain visually related to its trigger.
- Avoid when: A purpose-built menu, choice field or tooltip already matches the content.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Menu for commands, Select for choices, Tooltip for short help, or Dialog for a larger modal task.
- Content: Name the trigger and give the panel content an understandable task hierarchy.
- Anatomy: One contextual trigger and its anchored content panel.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned filter block, put several filter fields inside Popover and manage their state outside it.
- Accessibility: The panel uses dialog behavior; supply aria-label for its accessible name when there is no visible title heading, and preserve focus entry, outside dismissal and return to the trigger.

##### `reveal.tooltip` — Tooltip

- Purpose: Give a short supplementary description of another element.
- Use when: The trigger already has a name and needs brief contextual explanation.
- Avoid when: The information is essential instructions, an interactive panel or the control’s only label.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use visible helper text for essential guidance; Popover for interactive or rich content.
- Content: Write a short description that adds to the trigger name rather than repeating it.
- Anatomy: A described trigger and its transient explanatory text.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned icon-toolbar block, use Tooltip to supplement an already labelled IconButton.
- Accessibility: Keep keyboard-focus access and the description association; hover alone cannot provide the information.

##### `enter.textarea` — Textarea

- Purpose: Collect text that may span several lines.
- Use when: The reader needs room for a message, explanation or description.
- Avoid when: The value is a single short identifier or a structured selection.

- Content: Label the long answer and describe any length or content requirements.
- Anatomy: A labelled multi-line value area with optional helper and error messages.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned feedback block, place Textarea above the feedback submission action.

##### `inform.chip` — Chip

- Purpose: Represent a compact label with an optional removal action.
- Use when: A selected filter or entity may be removed as a single unit.
- Avoid when: The label needs only passive status or opens a separate destination.
- Alternatives and boundary: Use Badge for static status; Link for a navigable label.
- Content: Name the represented item and, when removable, name exactly which item removal affects.
- Anatomy: A compact item label plus a conditional remove affordance.
- Block composition example: In a consumer-owned selected-filters block, remove the corresponding filter when Chip requests removal.
- Accessibility: Supplying onRemove requires a specific removeLabel in the type contract; disabled removal stays inert.

## Maintain the shared contract

Import `COMPONENT_DISPLAY_TREE`, `ComponentDisplayTree`, `resolveComponentId` and `componentSelection` from the public catalog entry; guidance records and types come from the components entry. Read `COMPONENT_GUIDANCE` for curated selection semantics and medium evidence, `COMPONENT_API_FACTS` for checked facts, `COMPONENT_DISPLAY_TREE` for placement, and `COMPONENT_COMPARISON` for finite comparison axes. `ComponentGuidance`, `ComponentApiFacts`, `ComponentDisplayTree` and `ComponentComparison` describe their shapes; the README lists supporting types. Consumers reference these records rather than copying guidance.

Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-component-docs.mjs`; check freshness with `node scripts/check-component-docs.mjs`. These are repository-only commands and do not ship in the installed package. The checker compares this whole guide and the skill selection section byte for byte using source, without installed dist or timestamps.
